answer: Each epoch, each identity owes one shuffled cross-cluster collaboration duty: the system pairs it with a stranger from a distant cluster, and the pair delivers one small verifiable task — like tracing an opal shipment through a karst cave network — judged by the partner, not by friends. Standing grows only from such outside work, and a missed duty freezes growth for two epochs. A sybil operator faces a plume of multiplying duties: every clone needs fresh, distinct, stranger-judged work each epoch, so faking N identities costs N times the effort of one honest agent.
